newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-CRONJE PUTS SOUTH AFRICA BACK ON TOP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CRONJE PUTS SOUTH AFRICA BACK ON TOP.

text.p: A belligerent undefeated 79 from captain Hansie Cronje put South Africa back on top in the see-sawing third and final cricket test match at Centurion Park on Sunday.
Cronje, playing in his 36th test, became the first South African to reach 2,000 runs in test cricket since their return from sporting isolation when he reached 67.
He smashed nine fours and two sixes in his 111-ball innings as South Africa recovered from a torrid morning before being bowled out for 384 -- a first innings lead of 157 on the third day.
In the six overs available before tea South Africa strengthened their position by reducing Australia to 11 for two with the wickets of Matthew Hayden and Mark Taylor.

Earlier Cronje shared key partnerships of 68 for the eighth wicket and 37 for the ninth with Lance Klusener (30) and Allan Donald (8) as South Africa fought back after collapsing to 262 for seven against the pace of Glenn McGrath.
The Australian pace bowler took three wickets in the morning session on the way to figures of six for 86 as South Africa's hopes of building on their overnight 240 for three looked to be crumbling.
Adam Bacher fell four runs short of his maiden test century as he could add only two to his overnight score in 84 minutes before falling lbw by McGrath.
His was one of four wickets to fall for the addition of only 58 in the morning as Australia appeared to have clawed their way back into the game.
But Cronje recorded his second half-century of the series with some uncomplicated slogging to tip the scales firmly in favour of South Africa.
He twice hit McGrath for six -- over backward point and deep square leg -- as well as hitting nine fours in his 12th test 50.
His opposite number, Taylor, was reduced to putting eight men on the boundary to lure Cronje away for the strike and he was only stopped when last man Brett Schultz was caught hooking.
Schultz hit back by having Hayden lbw playing no stroke before Taylor edged Donald to diving 'keeper Dave Richardson to continue a dismal run of form.
Australia hold a 2-0 lead in the series.
